principles.statement: Multi-start SA with greedy local search and ILS perturbation, using adaptive restart scaling (1.5M fixed iteration budget, 30 ILS cycles), achieves 87.16% cut ratio consistently on Max-Cut with n<=1000, m<=20000. This is near the theoretical GW bound of 87.8%. Fixed restart counts (12 or 20) produce inconsistent scores due to TLE on large graphs.
principles.mechanism: SA explores beyond 1-flip local optima; ILS perturbation adds diversity cheaply; adaptive restarts prevent TLE. Combined, these achieve near-optimal cuts within tight time constraints.
principles.applicability_bounds: For graphs in this size range with ~2s per-test time limits. Larger graphs or tighter limits would need further budget reduction.

principles.statement: Do not use chrono/clock-based timing in Frontier-CS judge solutions — use fixed iteration counts instead.
principles.mechanism: The designer observed that chrono::steady_clock-based loop control caused score=0, likely due to judge environment restrictions or overhead. Fixed iteration counts with tuned alpha work reliably.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to all Frontier-CS algorithmic problems. May not apply to other judges.

principles.statement: The Frontier-CS judge for problem 192 produces deterministic scores for deterministic solutions (fixed RNG seed). Run-to-run variance of 0 observed across 2-3 consecutive runs for both tested solutions. Prior observed variance (84.62 vs 87.28) was anomalous, not systematic.
principles.regime: Problem 192 judge, deterministic C++ solutions with fixed seeds
principles.mechanism: The judge compiles and runs the solution on a fixed test set. With a fixed RNG seed and no time-dependent behavior (RP-2), the output is deterministic. Prior variance was likely due to different judge environments or test sets, not the solution itself.
principles.applicability_bounds: Assumes solution uses fixed RNG seed and iteration-based termination. May not hold if judge infrastructure changes.

principles.statement: Adaptive restart scaling (adjusting SA restart count by graph size with a fixed total iteration budget of 1.5M) achieves 87.16% cut ratio consistently with zero run-to-run variance, compared to fixed 12-restart SA+ILS which varies 84-87 due to TLE. The key parameters: n<=100->20 restarts, n<=300->12, n<=600->8, n>600->5.
principles.regime: Max-Cut with n<=1000, m<=20000, per-test time limit ~2s
principles.mechanism: Fixed restart counts ignore graph size: 12 restarts × 253K SA iterations = 3M total iterations. For large graphs (n>600, avg degree 40), each iteration touches ~40 adjacency entries, totaling ~120M memory accesses. This exceeds the ~2s per-test time limit. Adaptive scaling keeps total work proportional to time budget by reducing restarts for larger graphs.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to SA-based Max-Cut solvers with per-test time limits. The specific thresholds (1.5M budget, restart tiers) are tuned for n<=1000, m<=20000 with ~2s time limit.
